_comment: HQ Evolution external-discovery watchlist (spec section 9/43). Each topic must answer 'why is this relevant to TJR HQ?' before being searched — no generic tech-trend scanning. `gap_hypothesis` is exactly that — a HYPOTHESIS, not a settled fact — validated against current repo evidence by state_validation.py before any external search happens (`validation`, when present; omitted where no honest deterministic check exists, which validates as 'unclear' and still proceeds cautiously). github_query uses GitHub's search-qualifiers syntax (https://docs.github.com/search-github/searching-on-github).

topics.gap_hypothesis: core/model-router remains a bespoke, single-service router with no evaluated open-source alternative.
topics.validation_question: Does core/model-router/app.py (the bespoke router) still exist as the only routing implementation?
topics.why_relevant: HQ already runs a bespoke Model Router that self-improvement's own router_client.py depends on. A more mature open-source router could reduce maintenance burden or improve routing quality for the same workload.

topics.gap_hypothesis: HQ's episodic/knowledge memory is hand-rolled with no dedicated retrieval-evaluation harness.
topics.validation_question: Does a retrieval-evaluation harness exist anywhere under core/ or tests/ yet?
topics.why_relevant: HQ's episodic/knowledge stores (tests/test_episodic_memory.py, knowledge/) are hand-rolled. A proven memory architecture could improve recall quality or reduce the surface area HQ has to maintain itself.

topics.gap_hypothesis: Retrieval quality across findings/briefs/advisory is judged qualitatively, with no systematic evaluation harness.
topics.validation_question: Does a retrieval-evaluation harness exist anywhere under core/ or tests/ yet?
topics.why_relevant: deepeval's HallucinationMetric now provides a real evaluation harness for LLM-output quality (platform-runtime/lib/quality_scoring_service.py's score_output(), judge-model-backed via core/model-router since 2026-09-12), wired as a shadow-mode-only caller in build_learning_loop.py to prove it end-to-end. Narrows this gap; does not close it — score_output() only checks hallucination/faithfulness against supplied context, not retrieval quality itself (what gets fetched in the first place), and has exactly one caller so far, in shadow mode. No separate RAGAS/open-rag-eval integration needed for now.

topics.gap_hypothesis: Delivery channels (Telegram, Captain's Chair) may still perform independent LLM re-synthesis of the same intelligence instead of rendering one canonical Brief.
topics.validation_question: Does telegram-bots/xo/app.py's /brief command render the canonical intelligence_briefs row, or does it call its own separate LLM synthesis for brief content?
topics.why_relevant: Independent per-channel re-synthesis of the same intelligence (see spec example: canonical Brief vs duplicate channel narration) would mean redundant LLM calls; worth confirming whether that's still true before researching caching/synthesis-reuse patterns for it.

topics.gap_hypothesis: core/model-router/call_log.jsonl is a flat, unrotated, unaggregated append-only log with no queryable tracing.
topics.validation_question: Does any script or service rotate or aggregate call_log.jsonl yet?
topics.why_relevant: Arize Phoenix now provides live, queryable LLM tracing (deploy/phoenix.service, :6006, since 2026-09-12) — routing/latency/cost regressions are no longer invisible to operators. core/model-router/call_log.jsonl itself remains a separate, still-real gap: flat, unrotated, unaggregated, unbounded disk growth risk.

topics.gap_hypothesis: No browser-driven collection path exists — OSINT/technical collectors rely entirely on RSS/API polling.
topics.validation_question: Does any collector under intelligence/ or core/ use Playwright/Puppeteer/Selenium yet?
topics.why_relevant: OSINT/technical collectors rely on RSS/API polling; a maintained browser-automation agent could extend coverage to sources with no feed, if a real coverage gap is confirmed by Technical/Health OSINT findings.

topics.gap_hypothesis: MCP integration effort and fit are tracked ad hoc, not evaluated against a standard checklist.
topics.validation_question: Is there a documented MCP integration checklist or evaluation record anywhere in the repo?
topics.why_relevant: HQ already integrates several MCP servers; new MCP servers may close a specific integration gap (e.g. a data source Technical OSINT currently polls by hand) rather than being adopted for novelty.

topics.gap_hypothesis: There is no measured PR-acceptance rate for batch_coding.py's engineering-handoff pipeline.
topics.validation_question: Does scripts/self_improvement/metrics_template.py (or an equivalent PR-acceptance metric) exist yet?
topics.why_relevant: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED 2026-09-12: batch_coding.py's engineering-handoff pipeline was a single-shot coder with zero structural understanding of types/signatures/call relationships and no memory of anti-patterns or prior solutions — context_enricher.py's enrich() relied entirely on literal keyword overlap between the mission title and file names/bodies. core/engineering/context_enricher.py now additionally shells out to a locally-installed cortex_suite (github.com/Artistsyn/cortex_suite, offline Rust+tree-sitter MCP server pair, no API keys/network calls) indexed against core/, platform-runtime/ and lcars-portal/ (see .cortex/index-sources.json) for a budgeted structural-API packet, matched anti-patterns, and recall of prior solutions — additive to, not a replacement for, the keyword search. Gated behind CORTEX_CONTEXT_ENABLED (default on) and degrades to silence on any failure. Still open: this only adds INPUT context — the pipeline remains single-shot (one prompt, one diff), not multi-step task decomposition; a proven task-decomposition pattern (planning before coding, or iterative self-correction) could still improve handoff success rate if HandoffPRStrategy's PR acceptance rate is ever found to be low. Cross-language boundary detection (quartz-ctx's orphaned-route tracing between core/command-centre and lcars-portal) was scoped out as a stretch goal and remains unbuilt.

topics.github_query: local llm inference server efficient quantized
topics.gap_hypothesis: No per-task-type cost/quality tradeoff review has been run against the Model Router's TASK_POLICY.
topics.validation_question: Does a cost/quality tradeoff review for TASK_POLICY's cloud-routed task types exist anywhere in docs/?
topics.why_relevant: Any task_type currently routed to a paid model in TASK_POLICY could move to a capable local model if quality holds, directly lowering per-call cost.
